note: How `skynet setup --robot <model>` turns a model name into a driver library, and how far each driver has been tested. Kinds: prebuilt (builds with make alone; the wizard uses it built, or says how to build it), sdk (links a vendor SDK named in sdk; used built, or refused with the variable), cargo (a Rust driver in the workspace; found in the checkout's target/release, or refused with the cargo command for crate), sim (simulation-only; refused with the reason), python (runs under drivers/python-host; refused with the pointer), host (python-host itself: not a robot), library (shared code other drivers link: not a robot), unmapped (no install mapping yet; refused with the README). Shipped in release bundles so the refusals work without a checkout. lib is always the Linux name: a library built on Windows or macOS will not run on the robot. Release stages (DRY-COVERAGE-PLAN.md Decisions 19): every driver that commands a physical robot carries a stage — alpha (never run on a physical robot; dry-tested only against counterparts written in this repository), beta (never run on a physical robot; dry-tested against software this repository did not write that speaks the robot's own interface — the maker's controller software, the maker's simulator, or an independent implementation of the protocol — which substrate names as the command the nightly substrate workflow runs) or stable (has run on a physical robot; no driver has, and tools/check-release-stages.mjs refuses the word until one does). tested_against says what the stage rests on. A driver that hosts other vendors' code per body (ros2_control) carries bodies instead, each with its own stage. hardware false marks a body that drives no hardware by design (mock, pendant), which carries no stage.

fairino.tested_against: a simulated FR controller written in this repository, driven by FAIR INNOVATION's own FRRobot client. The maker's SimMachine simulator is a Windows virtual machine behind a registration wall, and has not been run

lite3.sdk: LITE3_SDK (Deep Robotics' headers and client, MIT, not vendored)
lite3.tested_against: a simulated motion host written in this repository, driven by Deep Robotics' own Sender and Receiver. No Lite3 simulator exists, and four command codes are read out of the vendor's compiled library

unitree.tested_against: Unitree's own simulator, unitree_mujoco, unmodified, for the Go2, H1, G1 and H1-2: stand, motion, hold and stop in physics

x1.sdk: X1_INFER (the vendor's built tree) and ROS_ROOT (a ROS 2 install)
